answer: One person should not become many voices. Give every newcomer a public portfolio of verifiable jobs, and let strangers re-audit a random sample each season. A climber who fakes a summit log, a dune survey, or a tundra repair will fail when an unrelated auditor re-checks the record and the beneficiary. Honest portfolios survive; forged ones collapse, and the forger loses standing and rewards tied to that identity. Because the sample is random and auditors rotate, running many fakes means maintaining many real histories at once, which costs more than it can repay.
